clue.text: Secret to reveal about foreign article

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for reveal wraps round the article

blocks.note: to reveal is to lay bare
der is the German definite article

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to expose a foreign newspaper story that was kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign article' means an article in another language; here German, whose masculine 'the' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Undercover work is done in secret, so the adjective stands for something covert or hidden.

clue.text: Tolkien's villains about to turn left among sportsmen in disorder

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the villains are read from the back
among puts the turn and the left inside the sportsmen

blocks.note: orcs are the monstrous foot soldiers of The Lord of the Rings
the Football Association, the body of English footballers

explanation.surface: Tolkien's orcs, on the point of turning left, find themselves in a disorderly scrum of athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition. 'Turn' gives its letter from the U-turn, and the FA is England's Football Association.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrofula is an old name for tuberculosis of the lymph glands of the neck, a medical disorder.

clue.text: Jamesian villain - one held to be dated

indicators.note: one is held by the villain, so it goes inside his name

blocks.note: Peter Quint, the ghostly villain of Henry James's The Turn of the Screw

explanation.surface: A literary note on a Henry James villain who is thought to be old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: A inside QUINT gives QUAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaint describes something attractively old-fashioned, so it can stand for dated.

clue.text: Does a sunrise issue from your idol's?

definitions.text: Does a sunrise issue from your idol's?

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written, then read upwards

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether the sun really shines out of the backside of someone you idolise.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the saying that an admirer thinks the sun shines out of their hero's backside; A plus a rising SUN spells the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue alludes to the idiom about worship, pointing at the bodily opening the sun supposedly shines from.

clue.text: Dessert with largely tasteless, cold, scabby skin

indicators.note: largely means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An unappetising pudding: bland, cold and with a scabby skin on top.
explanation.walkthrough: BLAN(D) + C + MANGE gives BLANCMANGE; the skin on a cold pudding makes a nasty, apt picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Blancmange is a sweet set milk pudding served as a dessert.

clue.text: Perform - or improvise on - Bach's first bit of framework

indicators.note: the first of the composer's name means its opening letter alone

blocks.note: musicians jam when they improvise together
the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A musician's choice: play Bach straight, or riff on his opening phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: DO + OR + JAM + B gives DOORJAMB; the musical surface hides a piece of joinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorjamb is the upright side post of a door frame, one part of the framework round it.

clue.text: Old flame turned up in unfinished house in jacket

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from bottom to top
unfinished means the last letter is lost
the old flame sits inside the royal house

explanation.surface: A former lover shows up at a half-built house wearing a smart jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: XE inside TUDO(R) gives TUXEDO. The Tudors were the English royal dynasty of Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuxedo is a dinner jacket worn for formal evening dress.

clue.text: Decimal system said to be moist

indicators.note: said means we go by how the name is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: the Dewey Decimal System classifies library books

explanation.surface: A librarian's joke that the book classification scheme is damp.
explanation.walkthrough: Dewey, the library classification, sounds the same as DEWY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy means wet with dew, so it is a fair synonym for slightly moist or damp.

clue.text: No-go in state, no-go by day?

indicators.note: in places the word for go inside the state's abbreviation

blocks.note: a go or a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Something banned within a state, and forbidden in daytime as well.
explanation.walkthrough: NO + C(TURN)AL gives NOCTURNAL; the definition is cryptic, as a night creature does not go about in daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal animals are active at night, so for them daytime is when they do not move about.

clue.text: Egg provides measure of energy, not beginning to include beginning or end of 16

indicators.note: not beginning means the first letter of the unit is removed
either the first or the last letter of the named answer, which happen to be the same
to include means the shortened unit wraps round the chosen letter

blocks.note: the answer to 16 starts and ends with the same letter

explanation.surface: A scientific note about an egg, a unit of energy and a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: (J)OULE wraps V, the first and last letter of VLADIMIR NABOKOV, to give OVULE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovule is the structure in a plant ovary containing the egg cell, loosely a small egg.

clue.text: Did these glamorous people formerly play by ear?

blocks.note: otic means relating to the ear, so whimsically otics are those who go by ear

explanation.surface: A question whether these glamorous types were once musicians who played without a score.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke splits the word in two: people who once did things by ear. Otic is the medical adjective for the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotics are striking, colourful foreign-seeming people, such as glamorous dancers or performers.

clue.text: Creche in north Surrey reorganised

indicators.note: reorganised means the county's letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A daycare centre in the north of Surrey gets a shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where young children are looked after during the day, as is a creche.

clue.text: Press suit where suits are pressed

blocks.note: first meaning: to woo, pressing one's suit to a beloved
second meaning: a place where lawsuits are pursued

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests ironing clothes; the suits are a lover's suit and lawsuits.
explanation.definitionFit: To court is to woo someone, and a court is the venue where legal cases are argued.

clue.text: Splendid display with a sombre hairdo

explanation.surface: A grand show put on with a gloomy hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a hairstyle with the hair swept high off the forehead, named after Madame de Pompadour.

clue.text: Drunken hack almost lit pile of stamps

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the writer's word is dropped
drunken means staggering out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: A tipsy journalist sets fire to a heap of postage stamps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile' reads as the definition's noun, but it is fodder; the definition is 'of stamps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Philatelic is the adjective for stamp collecting, describing anything relating to postage stamps.

clue.text: The last book to bring joy to the cleric

explanation.surface: A wish to cheer up the vicar with the final book of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the joy first, but it is attached after the cleric when the answer is built.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelation is the final book of the New Testament, closing the Christian Bible.

clue.text: Writer and bookman to take Iliad off in 5s

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of sorts, so the letters are disordered
in places the jumbled letters between the two numerals

blocks.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
V is the Roman numeral five, twice

explanation.surface: An author and a literary man set off to remove Homer's Iliad in some fives.
explanation.walkthrough: '5s' looks like a cross-reference but means two Roman fives; the jumbled letters sit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was the Russian-American novelist who wrote Lolita and Pale Fire.

clue.text: I called round on the 5th of April for hospital equipment

indicators.note: the fifth of the month name means its fifth letter only
round means the word for called surrounds what follows

blocks.note: rang or rung, as on the telephone
the fifth letter of the month name

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned on the fifth of April about some hospital gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The 5th of April' looks like a date but means the fifth letter. I + R(ON L)UNG gives IRON LUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron lung is a large machine that helps a paralysed patient breathe, used in hospitals.

clue.text: Monarch regularly being chivalrous

blocks.note: K for king, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A king who is routinely courteous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' would usually pick alternate letters, but here it is a synonym for NIGHTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Knightly describes conduct befitting a knight, the courteous ideal of chivalry.

clue.text: Dubious character's discount covers whore

indicators.note: covers means the reduction goes around the other word

blocks.note: a rebate is a partial refund

explanation.surface: A shady figure's price cut conceals a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: RE(PRO)BATE gives REPROBATE; the 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled scoundrel, the sort of person whose morals are questionable.

clue.text: South Africa gets into Italian food without a flashy performance

indicators.note: without a means one letter a is taken away from the food
gets into means the country's code goes inside

blocks.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: A South African tucks into a pizza without making a show of it.
explanation.walkthrough: South Africa's international code comes from Zuid-Afrika, its Dutch name, not the English initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Pizazz is showy flair and verve, the dazzle of a flamboyant performance.

clue.text: Super fish

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for excellent
second meaning: a European flatfish related to turbot

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for a fish; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is informal British slang, short for brilliant, and also a flatfish similar to the turbot.

clue.text: Islander gutted coastal town

indicators.note: gutted means its innards are removed, so middle letters go

blocks.note: the seaside resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: Someone from an island has destroyed a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the middle GH from BRIGHTON leaves BRITON.
explanation.definitionFit: A Briton lives in Great Britain, which is an island, so a Briton is an islander.

clue.text: Animal to stare into the distance? On the contrary

indicators.text: into the distance? On the contrary
indicators.note: the contrary reverses which goes inside, so the length goes into the staring word

blocks.note: to gaze is to look steadily
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: An animal gazing far off into the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says stare into distance, then reverses the instruction: ELL goes into GAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazelle is a small, graceful antelope of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Pedigree includes rising novelist

indicators.note: includes means the letters are found inside the word given
rising in a down clue means read upwards

explanation.surface: A writer on the up has a fine pedigree.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside pEDIGree, read upwards: GIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: André Gide was a French author, winner of the Nobel Prize for Literature.

clue.text: Descriptive term for what's essential in back support

indicators.note: in places the core inside the support
back means the support is read from end to start

blocks.note: a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: A name for the key element in a support for the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back support' reads as a brace for your back, but back reverses TEE. E(PITH)ET gives EPITHET.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is an adjective or phrase that describes a person, such as 'the Great'.

clue.text: Island where Nellie goes topless

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means losing the first letter

blocks.note: Dame Nellie Melba, the Australian soprano

explanation.surface: An island where a woman named Nellie sunbathes topless.
explanation.walkthrough: Nellie must be completed as the opera singer Nellie Melba; dropping her M leaves ELBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Mediterranean island off Tuscany where Napoleon was exiled.

clue.text: Practise religion of 12

blocks.note: to do is to practise or perform

explanation.surface: Practising the faith of twelve apostles.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a cross-reference to the clue for 12 but is just the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A dozen is a set of twelve items, so the number twelve defines it.

clue.text: Compiler's 20 involving bits of log in farcical situation

indicators.note: broken into bits, the word's letters are rearranged
involving means the answer to 20 surrounds the broken word

blocks.note: brio, liveliness, is a synonym of the answer to 20

explanation.surface: The setter's flair at splitting logs lands them in a ridiculous situation.
explanation.walkthrough: PIZAZZ at 20 points to BRIO. IM + BR(OGL)IO gives IMBROGLIO.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused, embarrassing tangle of events, the stuff of farce.
